commentary.speaker: play_by_play
commentary.text: It is minus eight degrees Fahrenheit in Minneapolis. The walker has selected a neighborhood loop and, against every available cue from nature, intends to repeat it.

commentary.speaker: color
commentary.text: The same neighborhood is back on screen. Not a replay error—he has simply chosen another dumb winter loop.

commentary.speaker: field_reporter
commentary.text: Five loops are in the books. Dad remains a healthy scratch: the tiny back-hall closet has won the matchup and will not release him for even one lap.

commentary.speaker: stats_desk
commentary.text: Eight verified returns through familiar territory. The neighborhood now knows the walker better than several members of his extended family.

commentary.speaker: play_by_play
commentary.text: Halfway: roughly eleven loops after a minus-eight-degree start, and the closet project continues to hold a commanding lead over father-son outdoor recreation.

commentary.speaker: color
commentary.text: Fourteen trips around the neighborhood. You could spend your time living, or you could inspect the same frozen blocks again, I guess.

commentary.speaker: field_reporter
commentary.text: Sixteen loops. Dad has still not appeared. Sources close to the back-hall closet describe the cleaning operation as extremely small and apparently endless.

commentary.speaker: stats_desk
commentary.text: Seventeen loops and counting. The course has changed tactically in one important respect: absolutely nothing.

commentary.speaker: play_by_play
commentary.text: OH MY GOODNESS, THE WALKER IS ALMOST AT THE FINISH—AND HE IS STILL WALKING!!!!! Twenty-one winter loops completed with no detectable increase in speed or judgment.

commentary.speaker: color
commentary.text: Twenty-two neighborhood loops, 26.36 miles, and zero appearances from Dad. The closet has claimed a clean sweep. History will decide whether an eight-hour walk that started at minus eight was the stronger use of time.
